questions.question: Why do many modern representation-learning methods L2-normalize feature and weight vectors onto a unit hypersphere before computing similarities?
questions.choice_A: To make similarity depend only on direction, removing confounding scale effects
questions.choice_B: To accelerate matrix multiplication on GPUs
questions.choice_C: To ensure gradients are always zero at the origin
questions.choice_D: To guarantee features are orthogonal

questions.question: Conceptually, what does cosine similarity between two normalized feature vectors measure in semantic embedding spaces?
questions.choice_A: The average Euclidean distance across all dimensions
questions.choice_B: The alignment of semantic directions irrespective of magnitude
questions.choice_C: The number of shared principal components
questions.choice_D: The ratio of their norms

questions.question: In angular softmax-based classifiers (e.g., SphereFace-like ideas), what is the key modification to the decision boundary compared to standard softmax?
questions.choice_A: It uses a quadratic boundary in the ambient space
questions.choice_B: It adds bias terms that shift class centroids
questions.choice_C: It bases decisions on angles between feature and class weight directions
questions.choice_D: It replaces cross-entropy with mean squared error

questions.question: Which statement best captures the intuition behind hyperspherical energy defined over a set of unit vectors?
questions.choice_A: It measures the total variance of features around the origin
questions.choice_B: It computes the number of nearly collinear triplets
questions.choice_C: It is the entropy of the empirical angular distribution
questions.choice_D: It penalizes small pairwise angles to encourage spread-out directions

questions.question: What property of cosine similarity makes it appealing as a semantic metric for normalized embeddings?
questions.choice_A: Scale invariance: it is unaffected by rescaling vectors
questions.choice_B: Translation invariance: it is unaffected by adding a constant vector
questions.choice_C: Rotation non-invariance: it changes under orthonormal transforms
questions.choice_D: Sensitivity to sparse noise in individual coordinates

questions.question: When weights are constrained to the unit hypersphere, what does a class weight vector represent in directional classifiers?
questions.choice_A: A learned covariance of the class
questions.choice_B: A prototype direction that defines the class angular region
questions.choice_C: A feature whitening transform
questions.choice_D: A bias correcting domain shift

questions.question: How does introducing an angular margin (e.g., in ArcFace/CosFace styles) influence learned representations?
questions.choice_A: It increases the feature norms uniformly across classes
questions.choice_B: It reduces the number of classes the model can represent
questions.choice_C: It enforces larger inter-class angular separation at a fixed intra-class compactness
questions.choice_D: It eliminates the need for normalization

questions.question: Which analogy is often used to build intuition for minimizing hyperspherical energy over many unit vectors?
questions.choice_A: Fourier series approximation of periodic signals
questions.choice_B: Graph Laplacian smoothing on manifolds
questions.choice_C: Low-rank matrix factorization
questions.choice_D: Repelling charges distributing on a sphere (e.g., Thomson problem)

questions.question: What is the main reason normalization can improve optimization stability in angular softmax frameworks?
questions.choice_A: It linearizes the loss with respect to logits
questions.choice_B: It prevents gradient explosion by clipping all derivatives to a constant
questions.choice_C: It decouples direction learning from norm growth dynamics
questions.choice_D: It guarantees convexity of the loss landscape

questions.question: In the context of hyperspherical energy, what does a low energy configuration typically indicate about a set of neuron weight directions?
questions.choice_A: They are clustered tightly into a few preferred directions
questions.choice_B: They are more uniformly spread, reducing directional redundancy
questions.choice_C: They have large and diverse norms
questions.choice_D: They align with principal components of the input covariance

questions.question: Consider two normalized feature vectors with cosine similarity 0.95. Which interpretation aligns with angular metrics as semantic measures?
questions.choice_A: The features are orthogonal and semantically unrelated
questions.choice_B: The features are identical in magnitude but opposite in direction
questions.choice_C: The features point to very similar semantic directions
questions.choice_D: The features have maximally different norms

questions.question: How does the notion of hyperspherical energy connect to redundancy among neurons in a layer?
questions.choice_A: High energy suggests many neurons are nearly collinear, implying redundancy
questions.choice_B: Low energy implies neurons share identical receptive fields
questions.choice_C: Energy is independent of angular correlations, so it cannot reveal redundancy
questions.choice_D: Redundancy is determined only by norms, not energy

questions.question: Why might researchers prefer angular decision boundaries for classification in high-dimensional embedding spaces?
questions.choice_A: Angles are robust to global feature scaling and emphasize relative orientation
questions.choice_B: Angles maximize within-class variance
questions.choice_C: Angular losses require no tuning hyperparameters
questions.choice_D: Angles eliminate class imbalance effects

questions.question: Which design choice helps ensure that class separation is governed primarily by angles in models like SphereNet?
questions.choice_A: L2-normalizing both features and class weights, optionally with a fixed scale
questions.choice_B: Using dropout on the final layer only
questions.choice_C: Replacing ReLU with sigmoid activations
questions.choice_D: Training with unlabeled data exclusively

questions.question: What is a common functional form for pairwise interactions in hyperspherical energy definitions?
questions.choice_A: A penalty increasing as the angle between vectors decreases
questions.choice_B: A reward for vectors becoming more collinear
questions.choice_C: A term that depends only on vector norms
questions.choice_D: A penalty on triple-wise angular sums

questions.question: If a set of class weight directions forms an approximately uniform spherical code, what downstream effect is typically expected?
questions.choice_A: Lower inter-class angular margins
questions.choice_B: Higher confusion between semantically dissimilar classes
questions.choice_C: More consistent decision boundaries and reduced overlap between classes
questions.choice_D: Inability to scale to many classes

questions.question: How does temperature scaling (or a fixed logit scale $s$) interact with angular softmax losses on the unit sphere?
questions.choice_A: It rescales angular logits to control the sharpness of class posteriors
questions.choice_B: It changes the optimal angular margin between classes
questions.choice_C: It adds a bias that shifts decision boundaries
questions.choice_D: It prevents features from being normalized

questions.question: What geometric structure do angular-margin methods implicitly encourage for intra-class features on the unit hypersphere?
questions.choice_A: Concentration around a class direction within a small angular cap
questions.choice_B: Uniform distribution across all directions
questions.choice_C: Alignment with orthogonal axes only
questions.choice_D: Periodic tiling of the sphere

questions.question: Which observation best links hyperspherical energy minimization with network interpretability?
questions.choice_A: Minimizing energy disperses neuron directions, making individual neuron roles less identifiable
questions.choice_B: Minimizing energy promotes diverse, less redundant directions that can map to distinct semantic factors
questions.choice_C: Energy minimization guarantees sparse activations across layers
questions.choice_D: Energy minimization aligns neurons with the top eigenvectors of the data covariance

questions.question: In practice, why might strict minimization of hyperspherical energy be counterproductive for a supervised classifier?
questions.choice_A: It forces feature norms to zero
questions.choice_B: It can overly decorrelate directions needed to model fine-grained class cluster structure
questions.choice_C: It prevents convergence of stochastic gradient descent
questions.choice_D: It eliminates the need for labels, reducing supervision signal
